# dagsterplus_concurrency_pool (Resource)

Manages a concurrency pool limit for a Dagster+ deployment. A pool is a named concurrency key; assets and ops assigned to the pool (via the `pool=` argument in your Dagster code) share the configured limit of in-progress executions. On destroy, the explicit limit is removed and the pool reverts to the deployment's default pool limit.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Limit the "database" pool to a single in-progress execution at a time.
# Assets/ops assigned to this pool in your Dagster code (e.g. @dg.asset(pool="database"))
# will share this limit.
resource "dagsterplus_concurrency_pool" "database" {
  deployment = "prod"
  name       = "database"
  limit      = 1
}

# A pool allowing more concurrency for a less contended resource.
resource "dagsterplus_concurrency_pool" "external_api" {
  deployment = "prod"
  name       = "external_api"
  limit      = 25
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `deployment` (String) The name of the deployment the pool belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `limit` (Number) The maximum number of in-progress executions allowed for the pool (0-1000).
- `name` (String) The pool name (concurrency key). Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the form '{deployment}/{name}'.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a concurrency pool using '{deployment}/{name}' as the ID
terraform import dagsterplus_concurrency_pool.database prod/database
```
